messages:
maria: Quick check — noticed a mismatch between Python SDK and REST contract on /v1/generate. Python sends `model_name` when set, but the REST server expects `modelName`. TS SDK sends `modelName`. Any concerns about backwards compat?

kevin: Ugh, yeah that casing difference causes our request parser to ignore the field (falls back to default model). Saw a couple of telemetry spikes where customers ended up using `default-2025` unexpectedly. :grimacing:

jun: Can you paste a minimal repro? I want to confirm whether the server treats unknown snake_case fields as ignored or if we do a fallback mapping.

maria: Repro is tiny — from Python client:```json
{"prompt":"hello","model_name":"redwood-3b"}
``` REST payload we validate is expecting:```json
{"prompt":"hello","modelName":"redwood-3b"}
``` When Python omits `modelName` the handler uses the tenant default.

kevin: For defaults, TS SDK currently sets `modelName: opts.model ?? 'redwood-3b'` before sending. Python leaves `model_name` as None and marshals as `null` (we recently changed None->null behavior). That also differs from omitting the field.

sarah: From QA: sending `null` and omitting produce different server paths (null -> explicit unset -> fallback; missing -> use routing default). We have a sticky bug where null bypasses some validation.

jun: Ok that explains it. Two separate issues: 1) naming/casing mismatch, 2) None/null vs missing semantics. Both can be breaking.

maria: Proposal: add a compatibility shim in the Python SDK that maps snake_case -> camelCase for top-level known fields before serializing, and change Python client to omit keys with value None rather than sending null for optional params.

kevin: I support both. Mapping should be opt-out via client config `compat_map: true` (default true for now). Need to flag in changelog and bump minor. Also open a server ticket to make server accept both casings for a migration window.

jun: I'll open a server-side issue to accept both keys for 3 months and add request logging to find affected tenants. PR #4821 from kevin could add the Python shim.

kevin: Drafted the PR, tests included — it currently strips None keys and maps `model_name`->`modelName`, `max_tokens`->`maxTokens`, `temperature`->`temperature` (same). Link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/4821 :eyes:

maria: Nice. Can we also add a short e2e test that simulates an existing customer sending `model_name: null`? Ensure server still picks tenant default as expected.

jun: Yep I'll add an integration toggle and run against canary. deploy-bot: scheduled canary run for this morning.

deploy-bot: Canary job queued for eng-platform-canary - run id cny-20260317-11. Results expected in ~20m. :rocket:

sarah: If canary looks good, set release note: "Python SDK: ensure param casing and omission semantics match REST; shim enabled by default for one minor release". I'll prepare the QA checklist.

maria: Thanks all — I'll leave the ticket to kevin + jun. Ping me on PR review when ready. :thumbsup:
